title: Azure YAML validation test only parses the header (strips everything from `stages:` on), so it cannot catch body indentation defects
description: The sole structural-parse test for azure_devops_yml does `raw.split('\nstages:')[0] + '\nstages: []'` and only yaml.safe_load()s the header, discarding the entire stages body. This is why the production-deploy env: indentation bug (see other finding) is invisible to CI. The analogous GitLab test (test_all_targets_parse, tests/test_scaffold.py:862-866) parses the FULL document for every target via yaml.safe_load(gitlab_ci_yml(target)); the Azure equivalent was deliberately weakened to header-only, creating a coverage hole precisely over the broken region. A full-document parse loop over TARGETS (mirroring the GitLab test) would fail today and is the correct regression test.
evidence: tests/test_scaffold.py:884-886: `raw = azure_devops_yml(target); header = raw.split('\nstages:')[0] + '\nstages: []'; doc = yaml.safe_load(header)`. No test ever calls yaml.safe_load on the unmodified azure_devops_yml(...) output. Replacing with `yaml.safe_load(azure_devops_yml(target))` for each target raises ScannerError (confirmed for all 7 targets).
